work_completed: Worker /mcp is now an OAuth 2.1 protected resource via @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider 1.4.0 (DCR + CIMD, PKCE S256, RFC 9728/8414 discovery, 1h access tokens, 7-day grants matching the Access session).

Sign-in goes through a Cloudflare Access for SaaS (OIDC) application: consent page first (MCP confused-deputy guidance), then Access with PKCE and a browser-bound single-use state, then ID-token verification (RS256 via JWKS, iss, aud, exp/nbf/iat).
Legacy ASFDK_API_TOKEN still accepted on /mcp through resolveExternalToken (constant-time compare); /agents/* keeps its static-token gate unchanged.
Added docs/mcp-oauth-cloudflare-access.md, .dev.vars.example, README and src/CLAUDE.md updates, and 22 unit tests.
blockers: The Worker cannot start on main or on this branch unless RRT_BEHAVIORAL_TOKEN_KEY is set: @neurolift-technologies/rrt-advocate@0.1.1 calls randomBytes at module scope, which the Workers runtime forbids. Documented as a required secret; the lasting fix belongs in rrt-advocate.

npm ci fails on main with ERESOLVE (agents@0.20.1 wants @cloudflare/codemode>=0.5, @cloudflare/think@0.10 pins ^0.4). npm ci --force installs the lockfile as-is; --legacy-peer-deps omits peers that the Worker bundle needs.
The existing self-hosted Access application covers the whole Worker, so MCP clients would hit the Access login page instead of OAuth until it is removed or narrowed to /agents.
decisions_made: Access for SaaS (OIDC) as the upstream identity provider, following Cloudflare's documented pattern for workers-oauth-provider, instead of validating the self-hosted app's Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion on /authorize.
OAuth resource derived from the request origin (one provider per origin), so workers.dev, previews, custom domains and wrangler dev need no extra config.
Only identity claims (sub, email, name) are kept in grant props; the Access access token is discarded.
Refresh-token lifetime 7 days to match the Access application's 168h session.
OAUTH_KV binding without an id so wrangler provisions a dedicated namespace on deploy, instead of sharing the SESSION/GOVERNANCE namespace.
